description: T27 (issue #106): MySQL stored routine static body audit. CREATE/ALTER/DROP PROCEDURE and CREATE/ALTER/DROP FUNCTION are audited lifecycle operations on the three MySQL anchors; BEGIN..END bodies fold statically bounded members (DML, SET, single-statement bodies) into the shared statement machinery with preserved line/column positions, while compound members (IF/WHILE/LOOP/REPEAT/CASE), RETURN, EXECUTE and parameter lists stay explicit unsupported evidence — never guessed. Client DELIMITER wrappers are client framing only: stripped from parser input with byte/line offsets preserved. TiDB keeps all six operations behind an explicit vendor boundary. Database verification proves the audited routine syntax is native-official on MySQL 5.7/8.0/8.4 and that the audit itself creates no routine (post_verify zero before the driver executes one).
